“The effects of the coronavirus will weigh on economic activity in the near term and pose risks to the economic outlook.” That said, the FOMC’s swift move to the effective lower bound, large-scale purchases of Treasuries and agency MBS, expanded repo operations, and dollar swap lines are textbook countercyclical tools that the literature shows can dampen downturns by easing credit frictions and reducing external finance premia (credit/agency cost channel: Oliner and Rudebusch, 1996a; contractionary policy raises the external finance premium, so expansionary policy lowers it). Term-structure evidence suggests asset purchases and lower short rates reduce term premia and support financial conditions (Ang and Piazzesi, 2003; Rudebusch and Wu, 2008). With market-based inflation compensation down but survey-based expectations little changed, anchored expectations in an inflation-forecast-targeting framework help limit deflation risks (Svensson, 1997a; Svensson and Woodford, 1999). Overall, the near-term outlook is negative, but the policy response meaningfully mitigates downside risks.
